subject: Information Theory
title: Hash Functions for Integrity
description: A micro-lesson that makes Hash Functions for Integrity usable.

hook.text: SHA-256 produces a 256-bit fingerprint. Change one bit in a 10 GB file and the hash changes completely.

buildup.text: Cryptographic hashes map arbitrary data to fixed-size digests. They're designed to catch any modification.

discovery.text: The avalanche effect: flipping one input bit changes about half the output bits. Tiny changes are amplified.

twist.text: Hashes detect tampering but can't detect accidental noise as efficiently as CRCs. Different tools for different jobs.

climax.text: Git, blockchain, and software distribution all use cryptographic hashes to ensure data integrity.

punchline.text: One bit changes everything. That's the avalanche effect.

quiz.question: What is the avalanche effect in cryptographic hashes?
options: A tiny input change alters roughly half the output bits
Hashes get slower with larger inputs
